label: a8-04-lem-successor-cardinal-exists
tail:
ALLEGATION_VERDICT: REAL_FATAL
ALLEGATION_LOCATION: items/lem-successor-cardinal-exists.md line 96, final sentence
ALLEGATION_ITEM_QUOTE: “the cardinal successor is always written ℵ(κ) on this page.”
ALLEGATION_TARGET_QUOTE: items/def-aleph-and-beth-hierarchies.md: “Notation rule, in force on this page and its companion. The superscript + means the successor cardinal only on a cardinal letter κ, λ, μ or an aleph.”
ALLEGATION_REASONING: The remark makes a universal claim about notation across its containing page, not merely within this lemma. A later sibling on that same page expressly defines the plus superscript on cardinal letters as successor-cardinal notation and declares that convention in force on the page and its companion. The companion example also writes aleph one as aleph zero plus. The contradiction is literal, so this is a fatal false claim in a Remark.

OTHER_FINDINGS: NONE
